resources.string: When enabled allows using the home button with a single press instead of a double press.
Thor Tools is made for the AYN Thor and also runs on the Odin 2. On other devices it can change settings the device doesn\'t expect. Continue at your own risk.

Thor Tools can\'t reach AYN\'s system service, so it can\'t change device settings. Check that \"Force SELinux\" is off in AYN\'s settings, then restart the app. A firmware update may also have changed the service.
Change the saturation of the display. Default value is 1.0.
Set up override when connected to an external display. Switch off to disable.
Used by Thor Tools to see which app is in front on each screen and to read button presses, for per-app settings, the AYN button and the quick panel.
Set up overrides per app. Switch off to globally disable app overrides.
Set while this app is in front; the earlier rate comes back exactly when you leave it.
The bottom screen goes off while this app is on the top screen, and comes back when you leave it. Saves battery in single-screen games.
The bottom screen stays on while this app is in front, even if it was off.
OdinTools handles controller style, L2/R2, performance and fan (see App profiles), so those rows below don\'t apply. Refresh rate and the bottom screen are Thor Tools\' own and still work.
Do you really want to delete this item?
You already added overrides for all your apps
Fan mode is required when setting a Performance mode
Delay applying overrides by 0.5s. This can help if apps crash when applying an override.
Adjust the maximum strength of vibrations & haptics. Switch off to disable vibrations.
Remap button to another key code

Keeps the battery between two levels while the Thor stays plugged in, which is easier on it. At the top level AYN\'s charging separation turns on: the charger runs the Thor and the battery rests. At the bottom level charging starts again.

Each switch is a charge setting change, which owners link to unstable charging. If the stability alert shows up after a switch, restart. A charger too weak to run the Thor drains the battery while it rests.
AYN\'s 80 %% charge limit is on, so charging stops at 80 %% and the top level (%1$d %%) is never reached. Pick 80 %% or less, or turn AYN\'s limit off in AYN\'s settings.
Charging separation means the power goes straight to the device, bypassing the battery. Notice that if the power source is insufficient, battery drain will occur.
Dump log output to a text file in the internal memory.
Log saved to %1$s in the internal memory
Couldn\'t save the log: AYN system access isn\'t available
Wi-Fi and Bluetooth off while it\'s closed, and back to sleep after an accidental wake.
Back on when the lid opens, if it was on.
Back on when the lid opens, if it was on.
Something in a bag can wake the Thor while it\'s closed: the charger, a button. Thor Tools lets the wake run out, then puts the Thor back to sleep.

After a wake with the lid closed, it waits as long as you set here. If the lid is still closed then, the Thor goes back to sleep; opening the lid cancels it. Wake it three times in a row to keep it awake.
Buttons, the controller and the touchscreens always work, and opening the lid always wakes the Thor. With an external display connected, a closed Thor isn\'t put back to sleep.
A separate app by Baggio94 that goes much further with sleep and the lid.
Installed. Switch each of these on in only one of the two apps.
Obtainium keeps it up to date. Pick SleepManager if it asks which file.
Nothing has happened yet: the lid hasn\'t closed with any of these on.
Last closed %1$s, opened %2$s: everything is as it was.
Last closed %1$s, opened %2$s: %3$s didn\'t come back on.
Lid opened: %1$s didn\'t come back on
Notifies you when charging keeps switching between rapid, slow and not charging while the charger stays plugged in, and offers a restart.
Warns when the charger connection keeps changing.
The charging state changed %1$d times in the last 10 minutes.
Charge limit automation is on and switches charging separation.
Owners report this often starts after a charge setting changed; restarting usually fixes it.
Save your game first. The device restarts right away.
How many switches within 10 minutes bring the alert.

Some Thors get stuck while plugged in: the status keeps switching between Charging rapidly, Charging slowly and Not charging, and the battery charges slowly or not at all. Many owners report it, often after a charge setting changed (AYN\'s 80 % limit, charging separation, a charge limit). A restart fixes it until it happens again. This alert notices the switching and offers the restart.
What helps, from owner reports: restart after changing a charge setting; a USB-C PD charger of 27 W or more and a good cable; charge to 100 % once before turning on a charge limit.
What\'s normal: with a charge limit, charging stops at the limit and starts again below it. On a computer\'s USB port (about 2 W) the Thor says Charging but barely gains while it\'s in use.
OdinTools is installed and can do this too, so Thor Tools leaves it off unless you turn it on here.
If charging acts up after a charge setting changed, here or in AYN\'s settings, restart once: owners report that brings it back.
A charge setting just changed. If charging acts up now, restart once.
Read every few seconds while this screen is open.
Android\'s Charging rapidly or slowly comes from what the charger offers: under 5 W is slowly, 7.5 W and more is rapidly.
Held: full, at a limit, or separation
Notifications are off for Thor Tools, so the alert can\'t be shown.
Device facts, a button tester and a report you can copy or save.
Tap Start, then press buttons. Home and the AYN button may not show up here; the system handles them first.
Choose which overlapping features Thor Tools handles while OdinTools is installed.
An older Thor Tools build is still installed under OdinTools\' package name and runs next to this one. Uninstall it.

These features change the same system settings as OdinTools and carry an OdinTools tag in their menus. While OdinTools is installed they start switched off here. You can switch any of them on. Turn the matching feature off in OdinTools first.
OdinTools isn\'t installed, so every feature uses its normal default.
OdinTools %1$s is installed and its app watcher is running.
OdinTools %1$s is installed. Its app watcher is off, but its startup actions still run.
%1$s\n\nSwitch it on in Thor Tools anyway? Turn the matching feature off in OdinTools first.
Per-app controller, L2/R2, performance and fan
OdinTools\' app overrides switch these too. If both apps do it, each one restores the other\'s settings at the wrong moment.
Controller style on an external display
OdinTools can switch the controller and L2/R2 style when a display is connected.
OdinTools can switch charging separation on and off by battery level.
OdinTools re-applies its own saturation value when the device starts. Only one app should do that.
Re-apply vibration strength after a restart
OdinTools re-applies its own vibration strength when the device starts. Only one app should do that.
What Thor Tools is allowed to do, with one-tap fixes
Thor Tools can change system settings through AYN\'s built-in service
AYN\'s system service doesn\'t answer. Turn off \"Force SELinux\" in AYN\'s settings, then restart.
Running: app profiles, the AYN button and the quick panel work
Not running. Tap to turn it on.
Allowed, so the charging alert and the running notice can show. Thor Tools grants this itself, so Android never asks.
Not allowed. Tap to allow them.
Exempt: Android won\'t stop Thor Tools in the background
On: Android may stop Thor Tools in the background. Tap to exempt it.
Listed, so AYN\'s task cleaner leaves Thor Tools running
Not listed. Tap to add Thor Tools.
Connected: swap screens, bottom-screen brightness and the controller lock work
Not connected. Tap to start it. Diagnostics shows why it stopped.
Not running while the accessibility service is off
Move through the panel with the D-pad and A. Off: touch only, the game keeps the controller.
Only the AYN button closes the panel
The panel stays open until you tap AYN or its close button: tiles, B, Back, Home and touches beside it leave it open. Off: those close it too, as before.
Access, hotkeys, the quick panel and a theme, one step at a time
A few steps get the most out of your Thor. Everything here can be changed later, and Skip leaves it all as it is.
A quick panel on the AYN button: modes, sliders, stats and widgets
Hotkeys on Home, Back, AYN and the volume keys, alone or in combos
Tools for the two screens: swap apps, Home on either screen, move the controller
Power management: what happens when the lid closes, and a charging alert
App profiles: controller, performance, refresh rate and more, per app
OdinTools is installed. Features both apps change start switched off here, so the two don\'t undo each other; Setup & diagnostics, OdinTools coexistence, explains each one.
Thor Tools allows most of this itself through AYN\'s system service. Tap the button, or one line at a time; Android only asks where it has to.
AYN\'s system service doesn\'t answer. Turn off "Force SELinux" in AYN\'s settings (it is off from the factory) and open Thor Tools again.
A tap of the AYN button opens the quick panel and holding it opens AYN\'s drawer. Pick a set of ready-made hotkeys to start from.
Nothing added: their keys are already in use.
Hotkeys you already have stay as they are. Controller & buttons, Hotkeys, lists and changes them.
The panel opens on the bottom screen. Pages and widgets are arranged in Quick panel, Edit panel.
For Thor Tools and the quick panel.
Display, Themes has previews, and makes your own.
A few more places worth a look:
Power management: pick what happens when the lid closes
App profiles: settings that follow each game
Quick panel, Edit panel: widgets in the sizes you like
Setup & diagnostics: run this setup again any time
Thor Tools sets this saturation again each time the Thor starts.
Thor Tools sets this vibration strength again each time the device starts.
Thor Tools has every setting OdinTools has, and more for the Thor. You don\'t need both, but they can stay installed together: here you choose which app handles each feature they share.

resources.string: Everything OdinTools does, built into Thor Tools: you don\'t need OdinTools for any of it.
Each app can set the controller style, L2/R2, performance and fan while it\'s in front. Thor Tools adds the refresh rate and the bottom screen.
Vibration strength and the charge limit came from the Odin 2; the Thor has the same controls.
Saturation, vibration, the charge limit, the external display style and app overrides, all built in
Thor Tools has every OdinTools setting and more. Choose which app handles what
Show what\'s playing here, with play, pause and skip.
Draw here with a finger. Type text in Edit panel.
What\'s playing, with play, pause and skip
Level, watts in or out, time to full or left
CPU, GPU and temperature over the last minute
Apps you pick, one tap to open
Draw on it with a finger, or type text here
No widgets on this page yet.
Delete page %1$d with everything on it?
Thor Tools may see what\'s playing.
Thor Tools needs to be allowed to see what\'s playing. Thor Tools allows it itself, as root, with one tap.
This page is taller than the panel; it scrolls.
The first page, as it looks on the bottom screen.
How some of the tiles behave.
Shows the panel on the bottom screen, to try it out
By default a tap of the AYN button opens or closes the panel and holding it opens AYN\'s drawer; change that under Hotkeys. The colours follow Display, Theme.
Open a game and its play time shows here
%1$s for %2$s now. Time for a short break?
The apps you open show up here
Thor Tools needs access to your pictures to show screenshots.
How long the app in front has been open, with a break reminder if you like
The apps you opened last, one tap to go back
Layout, L2/R2, lock and which screen has the controller; tap a line to change it
The time, a stopwatch and a countdown that keeps running with the panel closed
Your latest screenshots; tap one to open it
How full the storage and the memory are
The connection, Wi-Fi signal and ping
Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, airplane mode and Do not disturb
A note on the controller\'s screen when the same app has been in front this long, and again after each interval.
Thor Tools may read your pictures.
Thor Tools needs access to your pictures to show screenshots. Thor Tools allows it itself, as root, with one tap.
Shows the debug toolkit: quick checks of every action and of your hotkeys.

Each check reads the state, runs the action the way a hotkey would, checks what changed and puts everything back. Android\'s Settings app stands in for a game, so none of your apps are touched. Tap a row to run it alone.
Did \"%1$s\" do its job just now?
This closes every app in the background, as the real action does.
The screen turns off. Press the power button to come back.
The bottom screen goes off for a moment and comes back.
Swipe test: hands off, the swipes come by themselves
The accessibility service isn\'t running, so nothing can be checked.
Pick a type, then press your hotkeys of that type, in any order. Each row lights up when it is recognised; the presses below show what each one was taken for.
Off: recognised hotkeys do nothing, and the Thor\'s own buttons stay on this screen.
Hotkeys are being tested: they don\'t run until you leave this tab.
Only in chosen apps: try it there
You have no hotkeys of this type.
One file, rewritten each time, readable over USB (adb).
Set while this app is in front; the vibration you had comes back when you leave it.
Set while this app is in front (which swipes go: Extra tools, Gesture navigation); the page\'s choice comes back when you leave it.
AYN\'s own keyboard setting, close at hand.
The keyboard opens on the screen with the text field.
The keyboard always opens on the top screen.
The keyboard always opens on the bottom screen, so the top screen stays clear.
The keyboard setting didn\'t change. Thor Tools needs AYN\'s system access for it (Setup and diagnostics).
Turn Android\'s swipes off for good, or only hide the white home bar.
On: Android\'s swipes work as usual. Off: the swipes ticked below stop; get around with the Thor\'s Home and Back buttons, the quick panel and your hotkeys.
Swipe up for Home and Recents
Top screen; the bottom screen has none.
From either edge, on both screens. The bottom screen\'s home bar goes with it (AYN\'s own rule).

The ticked swipes stop while desktop controls are on for the app in front (the quick panel doesn\'t count as leaving them). About 2 s after they go off the swipes work again, unless the switch above or an app profile keeps them off.
For the switch above, Off with desktop controls, app profiles and the hotkey. One always stays ticked.
the hotkey, until the app changes
After a restart the swipe up for Home works again until Thor Tools has started.
Android didn\'t take the change. Thor Tools needs AYN\'s system access for it (Setup and diagnostics).
The white bar at the bottom of the screen. Hiding it doesn\'t stop the swipes.
Hide it on the top screen
AYN\'s own setting, also in Android\'s Settings under System navigation.
Turn the swipes off only while a game is in front: App profiles, Gesture navigation. A hotkey or a quick panel tile can switch them too (Gesture navigation on/off).
Colours, effects and battery colours for the rings around the sticks.
No stick lights were found on this device.
Thor Tools\' service isn\'t running, so the sticks won\'t change until it is.
Effects are drawn by the root input helper, which isn\'t running. Until it is, the sticks show the effect\'s first moment.
Colour, Off and Battery level go through AYN\'s own light settings, so they stay after a restart. Effects run while Thor Tools does. AYN\'s own puts AYN\'s settings back as they were.
AYN\'s own light settings light the sticks.
Tap a stick to give it its own colour.
AYN\'s own light settings decide, as if Thor Tools weren\'t here.
A steady colour on each stick.
The colour slowly brightens and dims.
A quick flash that fades, like a heartbeat.
Every colour in turn, the two sticks on opposite colours.
Red when the battery is low, amber in the middle, green when full.
Pick a colour, or mix your own.
This look picks its own colours.
How fast breathing, pulsing and the rainbow go.
The rings breathe green while the Thor charges and stay green once it\'s full.
An app can light the sticks its own way while it\'s in front: App profiles, the app, then Stick lights.
The big button on the front of the Wii Remote. Most games use it to jump, confirm or pick things up.
The trigger under the Wii Remote, pulled with your index finger. Games use it to grab, shoot or hold.
Small buttons near the bottom. Held sideways they become the main buttons: often run and jump.
Often a map, an item menu or pause.
Opens the Wii\'s HOME menu; the game pauses underneath.
The cross on top of the Wii Remote: menus and items, and walking when it\'s held sideways.
Aiming the Wii Remote at the TV. Here a stick moves the pointer instead.
Puts the pointer back in the middle of the screen.
A quick flick of the Wii Remote, often an attack or a spin. Here one button does the shake.
Tipping or rolling the Wii Remote, for steering, balancing and tilting the level.
Moving the whole Wii Remote through the air, like a sword or a racket.
The Nunchuk\'s thumb stick: walking and moving.
The small round button on top of the Nunchuk: often the camera or a second action.
The big trigger on the front of the Nunchuk: often crouch, lock on or shield.
Shaking the Nunchuk; only a few games use it, for a roll or a dash.
Laid out like the Thor\'s own buttons, so each letter goes to the same letter.
The shoulder triggers on top; a press here is a full pull.
The second pair of shoulder buttons, the lower triggers on a Classic Controller Pro.
The Classic Controller\'s thumb sticks: moving and the camera.
The Classic Controller\'s D-pad, for menus and 2D games.
Wii Remote in your right hand, Nunchuk in your left: most 3D games, like Super Mario Galaxy, Zelda and Metroid Prime 3.
The Wii Remote held flat like an old game pad: 2D games, like New Super Mario Bros. Wii, Kirby and Donkey Kong Country Returns.
The Wii Remote alone, pointed at the screen: menus, party and puzzle games, like Mario Party and Zack and Wiki.
The Classic Controller, a normal game pad: Virtual Console and the games that support it, like Smash Bros. Brawl and Xenoblade.
Turn the Thor\'s buttons into a Wii Remote, Nunchuk or Classic Controller profile for Dolphin.
Tap a Wii button to see what it does and change it. Under each one: its button on the Thor.
Pick one or more; any of them moves it.
Shares a Thor button with: %1$s. Both happen when you press it.
The Thor vibrates when a game rumbles the Wii Remote (its own vibration motor: the controller has none of its own).
This device has no vibration motor, so the profile leaves rumble out.
The suggested layouts follow RetroPup\'s “AYN Thor Ultimate Wii Setup Guide (2026)” on YouTube. Thanks, RetroPup!
Pointer stays where you leave it
Off: the pointer springs back to the middle when you let go of the stick.
Found %1$s: profiles go straight into its profile folder.
Found %1$s: profiles go straight into its profile folder, written by Dolphin itself.
Found %1$s. To save into it, give Thor Tools access to its folder once (below).
Found %1$s, but its folder can\'t be reached from here: save a copy and add it by hand.
%1$s is installed but hasn\'t made its folder yet: open it once, then come back.
Dolphin isn\'t installed. You can still save a copy to Downloads.
Dolphin already has a profile with this name; saving replaces it.
Left out of this profile: %1$s. Dolphin will show them blank; tap each to pick its Thor button again (Use the suggestion), or Reset this tab.
Dolphin has no Wii Remote profiles yet.
Straight into Dolphin\'s profile folder, checked, ready to load
Reset this tab to the suggestion
Saved as “%1$s” in Dolphin\'s profile folder and checked: Dolphin\'s owner, the right size, the same bytes. In Dolphin: Settings → Wii Input → Wii Remote 1 (Emulated) → Profile → %1$s → Load.
Saved as “%1$s”: Dolphin wrote it into its profile folder and lists it there. In Dolphin: Settings → Wii Input → Wii Remote 1 (Emulated) → Profile → %1$s → Load.
Saved as “%1$s” through Dolphin\'s folder access, but its folder doesn\'t list it yet. Open Dolphin\'s folder in Files to look, or save again.
Dolphin\'s folder needs your OK once. The picker opens in Dolphin\'s folder: tap Use this folder, then Allow. The profile is saved right after, and from then on every save goes straight in.
On: Dolphin itself writes each profile into its folder. Works without root.
Works without root. The picker opens in Dolphin\'s folder: tap Use this folder, then Allow.
Dolphin\'s folder access is on: Dolphin itself now writes each profile you save.
That wasn\'t Dolphin\'s top folder (the one with Config in it). In the picker, choose Dolphin and tap Use this folder there. If Dolphin has never been opened, open it once first.

The copy is in Download/%1$s/%2$s.ini. To add it by hand: copy it with the Files app into Dolphin\'s folder (Open Dolphin\'s folder in Files above, then Config → Profiles → Wiimote), or from a PC over USB. The folder: %3$s. Then in Dolphin: Settings → Wii Input → Wii Remote 1 (Emulated) → Profile → %2$s → Load.
Dolphin\'s folder couldn\'t be written (%1$s), so here is the way by hand.
The profile works in both of AYN\'s controller styles (Xbox and standard) and both L2/R2 modes, and rumbles through the Thor\'s own vibration.
To use a profile: Dolphin → Settings → Wii Input → Wii Remote 1 (Emulated) → Profile → its name → Load. Not in the list? Close Dolphin fully (swipe it away in Recent apps) and open it again.
A Dolphin shortcut while you play: turns the Wii Remote sideways, for games that switch to it. Hold the first button, press the second.
A Dolphin shortcut while you play: stands the Wii Remote upright, for games that hold it pointing up. Hold the first button, press the second.
Pick two different buttons; until then this shortcut is left out of the profile.
Opens at Dolphin\'s top folder; the profiles are in Config → Profiles → Wiimote
Switches desktop controls (the controller as a mouse and keys) on or off. Switched on, they work where they are allowed: on the top screen, in the apps the lists allow.
Use the controller like a Steam Controller in desktop mode: a mouse pointer in browsers and apps, never in your games

The controller works like a Steam Controller in desktop mode: a mouse pointer on the right stick, clicks on the triggers, keys on the buttons. On by itself where you want it, as you move between apps and screens.
In every app except the blocked ones, on the screen the controller is on.
Only in the apps you chose, on the screen the controller is on.
Tick the apps desktop controls are for (a browser, YouTube…). With none ticked they work in every app except the blocked ones.
Tick the apps desktop controls must never be on in, like your emulators and games.
Emulators and games, so the controller stays a controller there
On \"Never in these apps\": take it off there first
On \"Only in these apps\": take it off there first

They follow the screen that has the controller, and work on the top screen, where Android shows a mouse pointer. On the bottom screen, or on a screen showing a blocked app, the controller stays a controller; they come back when it moves back. An app can be on one list only. While the quick panel is open, the controller is a controller.
AYN\'s own mouse mode is on: it moves a pointer of its own, and its buttons fight these.

Tap a button to choose what it does while desktop controls are on. Hotkeys come first: a button a hotkey uses does the hotkey, and while you hold a button that starts hotkeys (like Home) the pointer and triggers wait. The D-pad, Home, Back and AYN stay as they are.
%1$s starts hotkeys (%2$s). Hotkeys come first: its job here happens when you let it go, and only if no hotkey used it.
Hotkeys use %1$s too (%2$s). Hotkeys come first: while that hotkey\'s first button is held, %1$s does the hotkey.
Not on this button: holding it already does something else (switching desktop controls, or starting hotkeys).
Left to the app, the button stays a controller button there.
L2 and R2 work as analog triggers here: they press once pushed past the trigger point (Triggers card).
A tap of Start does this. Holding it pauses desktop controls here (General).
Opens Android\'s keyboard for the text field in focus: click the field first.
For small targets: the pointer moves at about a third of its speed while this button is down. One button at most.
Holding Start for a moment pauses desktop controls where they are, and holding it again resumes them; the switch and the on/off hotkey stay as they are
Now: %1$s. A preset sets the buttons and sticks; your speeds stay.
R2 clicks, L2 right-clicks, L1 and R1 go back and forward a page; every other button stays the app\'s
Right stick pointer, left stick scrolls, R2 and R3 click, L2 right-clicks, L3 middle-clicks, A Enter, B Escape, X keyboard, Y Space, L1 Ctrl, R1 Alt, Select Tab, Start Escape
The same face buttons, triggers and sticks; L1, R1 and L3 stay the app\'s
B goes back, L1 and R1 go back and forward a page, Start shows the recent apps
Shoulders and triggers, with every speed back to normal
Left to the app, a stick works as it always does there (the left one moves between links like the D-pad).
The D-pad always stays the app\'s: it moves between links and buttons like arrow keys.
Apps see the sticks too: many (Settings, Thor Tools; not Firefox) move their highlight with the left stick while it points or scrolls.
Like AYN\'s mouse mode: the sticks only point and scroll, and apps don\'t turn them into D-pad steps. Thor Tools hands apps a copy of the pad without them while desktop controls are on.
How fast it moves, how much faster towards the stick\'s edge, and how far the stick goes before it moves.
Choose a button above and switch on \"Slow pointer while held\"
Android\'s own setting slows every mouse, this pointer too. Tap to set it back to normal, then use Speed above.
Android\'s own setting speeds up every mouse, this pointer too. Tap to set it back to normal, then use Speed above.
How the scroll stick turns pages.
No stick scrolls now: set one to Scroll under Sticks.
The page moves with the stick, as on a touch screen
Pushing the stick left or right scrolls wide pages
How far L2 and R2 go down before they press.
Switches desktop controls fully on and off, like this switch. Set here; it works like any hotkey.
Off on home screens and game front ends
While the top screen shows a launcher or a front end (Cocoon, iiSU, Daijishō, ES-DE, Pegasus, Beacon, AYN\'s launcher), or nothing at all, the controller stays a controller.
With the controller kept on the bottom screen, the right stick moves the pointer and the left stick works the bottom screen with the D-pad.
Desktop controls on/off has its hotkey in Desktop controls.

AYN\'s mouse mode moves the pointer with the left stick and drags the page with the right one. Thor Tools switches it on while desktop controls are on and off again afterwards; the buttons keep their jobs here. AYN\'s mode may give A, B and X jobs of its own too.
The pointer works the top screen while the controller works the bottom one.
Controller stays on the bottom screen

The D-pad and the buttons chosen below work the bottom screen\'s app as a controller; the pointer, scrolling, clicks and the other buttons work the top screen. After a click or a touch up there the controller goes back down, unless a keyboard is up. Not while the controller is locked to the top screen, nor with a never-in app on the bottom screen.
Buttons for the bottom screen, besides the D-pad
The others keep their jobs on the top screen. Ctrl, Alt and Shift work on keys there, not on clicks.
Desktop controls off: hold Start to switch them on
No text field in focus: click one first
RetroArch\'s menu look, speeds and controller hotkeys, its BIOS files and cheats, in plain words and saved for you.
Puts RetroArch\'s settings back as they were before Thor Tools\' last change.

Thor Tools changes RetroArch\'s own settings file (retroarch.cfg) the moment you pick something, so there is nothing to save. It only does so while RetroArch is closed, because RetroArch writes its own settings over the file when it quits. Before the first change, the file is kept as it was, as retroarch.cfg%1$s next to it.
Thor Tools needs AYN\'s system access (PServer) to change RetroArch\'s settings, and it isn\'t answering.
%1$s has no settings file yet: open it once, quit it from its menu, then come back.
RetroArch is open. Its settings can only be changed while it is closed, or it writes its own back over them when it quits.
RetroArch is closed (like swiping it away: anything changed inside RetroArch and not saved there is gone).
RetroArch didn\'t close. Quit it from its own menu (Main Menu → Quit RetroArch).
Saved in RetroArch\'s settings and checked.
RetroArch has changed its settings since, so there is nothing to undo.
Not saved: RetroArch is open. Close it, then pick again.
RetroArch\'s BIOS folder isn\'t there: %1$s. An SD card that is out or a different one? In RetroArch: Settings → Directory → System/BIOS.
No controller hotkeys are set in RetroArch, so there is no button to open its menu, save or quit while playing.
RetroArch doesn\'t keep what you change in its menus when it quits.
Thor Tools\' own hotkeys take %1$d of RetroArch\'s hotkeys, so RetroArch never gets them.
RetroArch\'s hotkeys were set while the controller had the other style (Xbox or Standard), so its face buttons are swapped now.
A new menu look shows the next time RetroArch opens.
Ozone: a list on the left, the settings on the right, like a game console\'s menu. Clear on a wide screen.
XMB: icons in a row across the screen, the PlayStation 3 way. Pretty, but a lot of moving around.
Material UI: a phone-style list with big rows, made for touch. Easiest to tap on the small bottom screen.
RGUI: a simple retro text menu drawn in the game\'s own resolution. The lightest of them.
Save RetroArch\'s settings when it quits
What you change in RetroArch\'s menus is kept when you quit it from its menu or with the Quit hotkey. Swiping it away doesn\'t count as quitting.
The Quit hotkey asks for a second press, so it isn\'t hit by accident.

PCSX-ReARMed and SwanStation start without a BIOS, but games are more compatible with one. Beetle PSX needs the one of the game\'s region.
LRPS2 needs one PS2 BIOS, any version, in pcsx2/bios. It recognises it by its contents, so its name doesn\'t matter. LRPS2 advises against SCPH-10000.
Sega CD games need the BIOS of their region.
Optional: the console\'s own start-up screen. Genesis Plus GX uses them with its \"System bootrom\" option on.
Beetle Saturn needs the BIOS of the game\'s region, Kronos its own copy in the kronos folder; Yabause runs without one.
Flycast runs without the BIOS. The arcade sets (zip files from MAME) are for NAOMI and Atomiswave games; their contents vary, so only their names are checked.
Optional. mGBA and VBA-M use it with their \"Use BIOS file if found\" option on.
Optional: the boot animation. Gambatte uses them with \"Use official bootloader\" on; SameBoy has its own built in.
Optional for DS games; DeSmuME uses them with \"Use External BIOS/Firmware\" on. melonDS DS needs the DSi files for DSi mode.
CD games need a system card. Any of them works, but some games don\'t run with some cards.
Neo Geo games need neogeo.zip from an arcade set (FinalBurn Neo also finds it next to the games). Its contents vary between sets, so only its name is checked.
NeoCD runs without one, but a real BIOS is the most compatible. It recognises them by their contents.

Pre-Beta, not perfect yet. It\'s made for playing games, where a HUD, a score or a logo sits in one place. Expect small side effects: a dark shadow can stay for a few seconds after something moves or goes away, and still parts of menus or home screens can look a bit patchy or dimmer. With Move, a thin dark edge can show beside the moved parts. If it bothers you, switch it off.
Tighter areas that keep their protection through small changes, each dimmed evenly by its brightness, checked twice a second. Still being tested.
AYN\'s shifter and refresher, as on AYN\'s page.

AYN\'s protection only runs while neither screen\'s picture changes: a game, a video or an animated home screen on either screen keeps it off. At exactly 1 second, AYN\'s shifter moves both screens every second whatever is shown, by a quirk of its timing. Thor Tools\' own shifter and refresher judge each screen on its own; while they run, AYN\'s are switched off and come back as you set them.
Off while Thor Tools\' pixel shifter runs, so the two don\'t fight. It comes back as you set it when you switch Thor Tools\' off.
Off while Thor Tools\' refresher runs by itself, so the two don\'t both run. It comes back as you set it when you switch that off.
